To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
roads are associated with increased forest plant invasion in the eastern United States.

(1) roads are positively associated with the occurrence of forest invasive plant species, (2) the effect of roads on forest invasive plant occurrence is greater than the effect of roads in the non‐forest landscape, (3) the effect of road density on invasive plant occurrence varies by species and region, and (4) the relationship between road density and invasive plant occurrence is strongest in regions of the eastern United States that are highly invaded.
roads have a significant effect on forest plant invasion in the eastern United States and the effects of roads are more pronounced in the northern portion of the study area.
